chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir Al-Mumineen (peace be upon him) said: 'When they cut off the relationships, the wealth is made to be in the hands of the evil ones.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the economic consequence of severing family ties according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this chain from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the spiritual sin of severing kinship ties (*qat' al-rahim*) to a tangible socio-economic consequence: the displacement of wealth from the righteous to the unworthy. This reflects the Shia understanding of divine justice, where moral decay in social bonds directly impacts material distribution, serving as a practical warning for the preservation of communal prosperity.
